tasks.short: Help site managers build budgets, understand costs, and agree how shared costs are allocated.

today.trigger: A site manager requests cost advice, an allocation changes, or a budget round opens.
steps: Pull AFAS actuals, payroll totals, and staffing agency costs into Excel.
Check cost centres and separate direct costs from shared costs.
Apply allocation keys and calculate budget requirements.
Discuss assumptions with site managers and resolve missing information.
Send the analysis and record agreed assumptions.
drudgery: Reconciling agency files with booked costs
today.time_sinks: Joining inconsistent exports and debating allocation assumptions across Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo.

lenses.faster: Refresh one controlled cost model instead of rebuilding spreadsheets. Produce allocation tables and a source-linked explanation from the same inputs.
lenses.autonomous: After a successful nightly extract, recalculate existing allocation rules and flag changes. New allocation rules and advice remain subject to approval.
lenses.ambitious: Give every site a monthly view of fully loaded costs and the effect of alternative allocation methods. Add cost per pallet or transport unit once reliable activity data is available.
lenses.joy: Remove copying, formula repair, and repeated reconciliations. Keep the conversations that help managers understand costs they can influence.
lenses.options: Compare allocation by headcount, floor space, and measured activity, with the effect on each site shown explicitly.
lenses.altitude: Own the allocation policy and model quality rather than operating individual worksheets.
reach: Controller: maintain management cost-allocation schedules.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: translate aggregated workforce plans into financial scenarios.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: model approved CAO cost changes.

tasks.human_edge: Managers need someone who can explain whether an allocation is fair, distinguish controllable costs, and challenge unrealistic assumptions.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: software calculates costs and allocations; an optional language-model step drafts explanations. The analyst approves advice because allocation choices affect site accountability.

in_practice.trigger: A structured request is submitted or a validated nightly extract changes the relevant costs.
steps: Load a dated AFAS snapshot and approved agency exports; reconcile totals and reject missing mappings.
Calculate allocations using versioned rules in Excel Power Query or a controlled calculation service.
Run alternative allocation methods and identify material changes.
Draft advice using calculated tables and approved SharePoint policies, linking each figure to its source.
The analyst checks assumptions with the site manager and releases the approved response.
in_practice.human_gate: The FP&A analyst approves each advice package; the Controller approves changes to allocation policy before they enter the calculation rules.
data_needed: GL accounts, cost centres, and reconciled actuals
Approved allocation keys and effective dates
Aggregated payroll costs by site and cost centre
Agency hours, rates, and invoice status
Payroll-approved assumptions for both applicable CAOs
Site activity measures supplied by operations
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint analysis register containing request, snapshot date, allocation-rule version, source references, exceptions, and approval.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors can retrieve administrator-selected records and fields; Noordhaven must configure the required datasets.
Power Query can join tables using matching columns, supporting repeatable cost and allocation preparation.
The proposed approval workflow, 60% labour saving, and 1.8 times elapsed speedup are untested estimates.

risks: A convenient allocation key may distort site profitability or reward the wrong behaviour.
Agency invoices and payroll actuals may cover different periods.
A language model may present an allocation choice as company policy without supporting evidence.
Employee-level pay or absence data may be exposed unnecessarily; use restricted, aggregated inputs under AVG/GDPR.
research_questions: What share of the 181 annual hours is repeatable calculation rather than manager discussion?
Are allocation keys documented, approved, and stable enough to encode?
Can agency costs and payroll totals reconcile to AFAS at site and period level?
Does a pilot reduce handling time without increasing allocation disputes or corrections?

tasks.short: Review site and department budgets and explain which trends will change the forecast.

today.trigger: The weekly budget review or monthly forecast cycle begins.
steps: Refresh AFAS actuals and collect the latest budget files.
Compare spending with budget, prior months, and the previous year.
Separate recurring changes from timing effects and one-off costs.
Ask managers about volume, staffing, fuel, and other cost drivers.
Update forecast assumptions and explain the main trends.
drudgery: Checking the same cost centres repeatedly
today.time_sinks: Collecting operational explanations and distinguishing real trends from late postings, seasonality, and incomplete agency costs.

lenses.faster: Calculate trend comparisons and driver bridges automatically. Start the review with ranked exceptions and unresolved assumptions.
lenses.autonomous: After each successful nightly refresh, update trend flags and candidate forecast changes. The analyst approves changes to the official forecast.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a weekly forecast of labour, agency spend, fuel, and site margin, with error measured against subsequent actuals.
lenses.joy: Replace spreadsheet assembly with investigation of surprising movements and useful conversations with operations.
lenses.options: Compare base, peak-demand, weak-demand, and labour-cost scenarios. Show which assumptions explain the difference.
lenses.altitude: Design the driver model and monitor its forecast errors rather than producing each trend comparison manually.
reach: Controller: prepare management variance analysis.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: develop aggregated workforce-cost forecasts.
Finance Director: prepare early warnings and forecast challenge questions.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges whether a statistical trend has an operational explanation and whether managers' forecasts are credible.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic calculations produce trends and scenario outputs, while a language model can organise manager explanations. Forecast changes require human approval because historical patterns do not establish business causes.

in_practice.trigger: A validated nightly extract arrives or an approved driver assumption changes.
steps: Reconcile actuals and mark periods with incomplete payroll, agency costs, or accruals.
Calculate seasonal comparisons and bridges using approved driver definitions.
Rank material deviations and attach source figures and existing manager explanations.
Generate candidate forecast changes and scenario ranges in a deterministic model.
The analyst challenges the explanations, approves assumptions, and saves the forecast version.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every forecast revision; the Finance Director approves the published business forecast.
systems: Excel Power Query and forecast model
data_needed: Comparable monthly actuals, budgets, and forecast versions
Calendar, working days, and seasonal assumptions
Aggregated employee and flex-worker costs
Approved CAO rates and agency contract rates
Reliable volume, productivity, and fuel inputs from operations
Manager explanations with owner and date
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint forecast register with input snapshots, model version, driver changes, explanations, approvals, and later forecast errors.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh; downstream analysis must check that the refresh succeeded.
Driver-based forecasts and historical error checks can be implemented using structured financial and operating inputs.
The proposed workflow, 70% labour saving, and 2.5 times elapsed speedup have not been measured at Noordhaven.

risks: Nightly data is mistaken for current-day visibility.
Missing operational volume data makes driver explanations unreliable.
A model treats correlation as a cause or extrapolates a temporary seasonal peak.
Detailed workforce analysis could reveal individual absence or performance; keep this forecast at aggregate financial level.
research_questions: How many months of comparable actuals and historical forecast versions are available?
Which operational drivers can be supplied reliably when no warehouse or transport system feed is specified?
Can a backtest improve the current forecast using the same information available at each historical forecast date?
Does the pilot reduce review time while preserving manager trust and forecast accuracy?

tasks.short: Check monthly department spending, investigate overruns, and agree actions with budget owners.

today.trigger: Monthly accounting reports arrive or a manager raises a possible overspend.
steps: Download department actuals and compare them with approved budgets.
Check large movements against invoices, payroll, and agency costs.
Ask the Accountant about missing accruals or incorrect postings.
Discuss genuine overspends and possible actions with budget owners.
Record explanations and follow up agreed actions.
drudgery: Scanning every department regardless of materiality
Looking up invoices behind recurring variances
Maintaining action lists separately from reports
today.time_sinks: Chasing explanations and determining whether an apparent overrun is a posting issue, a timing issue, or real extra spending.

lenses.faster: Generate reconciled variance tables and evidence links automatically. Review the material exceptions rather than every department line.
lenses.autonomous: Run expenditure checks after each validated nightly refresh and place exceptions in an owner-assigned queue. Spending restrictions and accounting changes need approval.
lenses.ambitious: Detect emerging overruns before month close, including agency hours incurred but not yet invoiced.
lenses.joy: Remove line-by-line scanning and invoice hunting. Keep the work of identifying preventable waste and agreeing workable actions.
lenses.options: For each confirmed overrun, compare revised staffing mix, timing changes, and a forecast increase with their service implications.
lenses.altitude: Set materiality rules and improve the expenditure-control process rather than manually searching for every breach.
reach: Controller: maintain the management exception and action register.
Accountant: identify candidate accrual gaps for accounting review.
Bookkeeper: flag invoice coding anomalies for investigation.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes poor control from justified spending and negotiates actions that preserve warehouse and transport service.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: rules calculate deviations and collect supporting records, but resolving exceptions involves accounting judgement and manager commitments.

in_practice.trigger: A validated nightly financial snapshot arrives, with a separate month-close review checkpoint.
steps: Reconcile department totals and combine actuals with available commitments and agency hours.
Apply approved materiality thresholds and flag missing or inconsistent data separately.
Assemble supporting transactions and draft questions for each exception.
The analyst confirms causes with the Accountant and budget owner and approves action records.
Refresh the action register and verify whether approved actions changed the next period's result.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves conclusions and actions; the Accountant authorises journals and the budget owner authorises operational spending changes.
data_needed: Approved budgets and latest forecast by department
GL transactions and permitted invoice references
Available purchase commitments and agency hours
Accrual status and close checklist
Materiality thresholds and budget-owner mapping
Prior explanations and open actions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint expenditure-control register with exception IDs, source transactions, reviewer decisions, action owners, and closure evidence.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors support retrieving configured records for a financial exception workflow.
Rules can calculate material variances and distinguish incomplete data from threshold breaches.
The proposed exception workflow, 75% labour saving, and three times elapsed speedup are pilot assumptions.

risks: Unbooked agency hours or commitments make spending appear lower than it is.
Thresholds miss many small overruns that together become material.
An accounting correction is counted as a genuine operational saving.
Automatic spending blocks disrupt service; this proposal only prepares exceptions and recommendations.
research_questions: Can incurred agency hours and purchase commitments be obtained before invoices are posted?
Would the proposed thresholds have detected the material overruns from the last six closes?
How much review effort comes from missing accruals and incorrect coding?
Does the pilot reduce investigation time without increasing missed exceptions or audit adjustments?

tasks.short: Check budget submissions for missing items, calculation errors, and compliance with approved rules.

today.trigger: A site or department submits a budget or revised estimate.
steps: Check that the submission uses the correct template and period.
Recalculate totals and compare assumptions with supporting records.
Check payroll assumptions against approved CAO and agency rates.
Review policy requirements and ask specialists about exceptions.
Return corrections and record the accepted submission.
drudgery: Finding broken formulas and inconsistent units
Repeating the same template correction requests
today.time_sinks: Following up incomplete submissions and confirming which policy or rate version applies.

lenses.faster: Validate required fields, totals, effective dates, and rate tables on submission. Present only failed checks and items needing specialist judgement.
lenses.autonomous: Routine checks run when a budget file enters the controlled submission folder. Failed submissions enter an exception queue before acceptance.
lenses.ambitious: Give budget owners immediate feedback before submission and apply the same checks to every forecast revision.
lenses.joy: Remove formula inspection and template policing. Keep the judgement about whether assumptions are defensible.
lenses.options: Show the effect of corrected rates, alternative start dates, and different agency-hour assumptions without rewriting the submission.
lenses.altitude: Maintain a versioned budget-validation rulebook with Payroll, HR, and the Controller.
reach: Controller: maintain budget submission controls.
Payroll Specialist: flag financial assumptions that disagree with approved payroll rules.
HR Business Partner: identify workforce proposals needing an HR or OR process check.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst recognises when a mathematically valid budget is operationally unrealistic or needs legal, payroll, or employee-representation judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: completeness, arithmetic, rate versions, and approval requirements are checkable rules. Specialist interpretation remains an exception rather than being decided by a model.

in_practice.trigger: A budget submission or revision is saved in the controlled SharePoint intake.
steps: Read the approved template and reject unsupported layouts or missing identifiers.
Recompute totals and check units, periods, mappings, and duplicate items.
Compare assumptions with effective-dated, specialist-approved rates and policy checks.
Record routine passes and route failures or ambiguous requirements to the responsible specialist.
The analyst accepts the corrected submission after exceptions are resolved.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine validation runs without approval; the analyst handles exceptions and accepts the budget. Payroll and HR approve rule interpretations and rate changes.
data_needed: Approved budget template and required fields
Chart of accounts and cost-centre mappings
Payroll-approved rates for CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO
Agency contract rates and effective dates
Delegation policy and approval requirements
HR-approved flags for proposals requiring an OR process
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint validation register with submission hash, check results, rule versions, exceptions, specialist decisions, and acceptance.

evidence.claim: Power Query can combine budget submissions with reference tables using matching columns.
Published CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer materials can inform Payroll's approved reference tables; Noordhaven's warehouse CAO must be supplied separately.
The proposed validation service, 70% labour saving, and 2.5 times elapsed speedup are untested.

risks: Outdated or incorrectly applied CAO rates create systematic budget errors.
Passing arithmetic checks is mistaken for full legal or policy compliance.
Valid unusual submissions are rejected by overly narrow rules.

A budget proposal involving a significant organisational change may require an OR advice process; HR must assess applicability. [SER advice rights](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/aan-de-slag-met-de-or/rechten/adviesrecht)
research_questions: What percentage of submissions already follow one stable template?
Can Payroll and HR provide approved, effective-dated rules for both CAOs?
Which past submission errors are detectable with explicit rules, and which require judgement?
Does the pilot catch all material errors in a historical sample without excessive false failures?

tasks.short: Work out the funding and cash needed for a site project or operational programme.

today.trigger: A manager proposes a warehouse improvement, transport initiative, or other investment.
steps: Clarify scope, timing, expected benefits, and who owns the proposal.
Collect comparable AFAS costs, supplier quotes, and workforce assumptions.
Build an Excel estimate of investment, operating costs, and cash timing.
Test benefit assumptions and identify missing costs with specialists.
Prepare the funding requirement and sensitivity analysis.
drudgery: Finding comparable costs in old files
today.time_sinks: Clarifying project scope and obtaining credible productivity, staffing, implementation, and training assumptions.

lenses.faster: Extract quote details into a checked cost schedule and reuse a standard project model. Calculate cash timing and sensitivities automatically.
lenses.autonomous: A completed project intake starts evidence collection and model preparation. The analyst approves the assumptions and funding estimate.
lenses.ambitious: Assess smaller site improvements properly and compare promised benefits with realised costs and outcomes after implementation.
lenses.joy: Remove quote transcription and formula rebuilding. Keep the investigation of whether a project will actually improve operations.
lenses.options: Compare staged implementation, leasing, outsourcing, and purchase where relevant, using consistent cash and benefit assumptions.
lenses.altitude: Own a reusable project-evaluation method and track which assumptions consistently prove wrong.
reach: Controller: prepare investment appraisal schedules.
Learning and Development Specialist: cost required training and certification capacity.
Finance Director: prepare project funding and liquidity scenarios.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst tests whether claimed productivity gains can be realised and asks for evidence when a project sponsor is optimistic.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: quote extraction and evidence gathering span several sources; deterministic software calculates funding. A person approves scope, benefits, accounting treatment, and funding assumptions.

in_practice.trigger: A project sponsor submits a structured intake with scope, timing, quotes, and an accountable owner.
steps: Retrieve permitted comparable costs and extract quote line items with document references.
Validate quantities, VAT assumptions, dates, units, and missing implementation costs.
Calculate investment, recurring costs, working capital, and cash timing using approved formulas.
Run scenarios for rollout delays, benefit shortfalls, and labour or supplier cost changes.
The analyst challenges assumptions with Operations, Accounting, HR, and L&D before releasing the estimate.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the appraisal; the Accountant reviews accounting treatment and the Finance Director authorises funding.
data_needed: Project scope, rollout dates, and sponsor
Supplier quotes and contractual payment terms
Comparable historical costs and current cash assumptions
Operations-approved volume and productivity assumptions
Payroll-approved labour costs and agency rates
Training costs, certification requirements, and available course capacity
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint project appraisal file with quote references, extracted values, corrections, model versions, assumptions, scenarios, and approvals.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors can supply configured accounting records for comparable-cost analysis.
Document extraction followed by numerical checks can reduce quote transcription work.
The proposed project workflow, 60% labour saving, and 1.8 times elapsed speedup depend on project-data availability and remain untested.

risks: Quoted amounts omit implementation downtime, training, maintenance, or working capital.
Estimated labour savings cannot be realised under actual shift coverage and service requirements.
Extraction confuses monthly and annual prices or amounts including and excluding VAT.
Projects affecting organisation or employment conditions need HR assessment of the relevant OR process before decisions.
Training completion data is used beyond costing; certificate eligibility decisions remain with qualified operational and L&D owners.
research_questions: Are past project appraisals and realised outcomes available for comparison?
Can Operations substantiate productivity and volume assumptions with measured data?
How much handling time is quote transcription versus scope negotiation and specialist review?
Does a pilot capture all material costs and reproduce independently checked cash schedules?

tasks.short: Summarise funding requests and recommend approval, revision, or rejection to the Finance Director.

today.trigger: A department or site requests funding outside, or within, an approved budget.
steps: Collect the request, cost estimate, and supporting justification.
Check budget availability and other claims on the same funds.
Assess cost, expected benefit, risks, and strategic fit.
Write a recommendation with conditions or alternatives.
Submit the pack to the authorised decision maker and record the outcome.
drudgery: Copying the same approval criteria into recommendations
today.time_sinks: Obtaining missing evidence and reconciling competing requests with the latest approved funding position.

lenses.faster: Build a consistent decision pack from the request and a reconciled funding balance. Draft the recommendation and conditions for analyst review.
lenses.autonomous: Submission triggers completeness checks, balance calculations, and a draft paper. A person approves every recommendation and funding decision.
lenses.ambitious: Compare requests as a portfolio, including trade-offs, cash constraints, and benefits realised from earlier approvals.
lenses.joy: Remove document assembly and repeated balance checks. Keep the judgement about which requests deserve scarce funds.
lenses.options: Present approve, approve with conditions, stage, defer, and reject options where they are credible, showing cost and service consequences.
lenses.altitude: Maintain the funding criteria and monitor decision quality rather than writing each paper from scratch.
reach: Finance Director: prepare funding prioritisation options.
Controller: maintain decision evidence and budget availability checks.
Accountant: prepare approved funding information for accounting follow-up.

tasks.human_edge: A person weighs strategic trade-offs, challenges sponsors, and takes responsibility for the recommendation.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: software assembles evidence and calculates availability, and a language model drafts options. Funds are neither approved nor rejected automatically.

in_practice.trigger: A funding request enters the controlled SharePoint intake.
steps: Validate the request against required evidence and the delegation policy.
Calculate available funds from the approved budget, spending, commitments, and recorded reservations.
Prepare comparable options and draft a recommendation with evidence references and unresolved questions.
The analyst checks the financial case and submits the approved recommendation to the authorised approver.
Record the decision and, after approval, update the controlled funding reservation register.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every recommendation; the authorised budget holder or Finance Director makes the funding decision. An OR process is completed first where applicable.
data_needed: Request amount, purpose, timing, and sponsor
Approved budgets, actuals, commitments, and reservations
Investment and liquidity assumptions
Funding criteria and delegation limits
Supporting appraisal and alternatives
HR confirmation of any required OR process
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint funding register with request ID, evidence snapshot, draft and approved recommendation, decision maker, conditions, and reservation changes.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors can provide configured financial records used in funding availability calculations.
The OR has advice rights for certain significant investments and organisational changes; applicability needs assessment.
The proposed decision-pack workflow, 65% labour saving, and two times elapsed speedup are estimates rather than documented outcomes.

risks: Concurrent requests consume the same apparent funding unless reservations are controlled.
A persuasive draft hides uncertain benefits or missing evidence.
The workflow bypasses delegation limits or a required OR process.
Nightly AFAS balances do not include every current commitment; show the snapshot date and separately recorded reservations.
research_questions: Is there one authoritative register of commitments and funding reservations?
Can approval limits and mandatory evidence be encoded without ambiguity?
Do historical recommendations contain enough evidence to evaluate draft quality independently?
Does the pilot reduce preparation time while preserving decision quality and approval compliance?

tasks.short: Organise regular budget packs and special analyses, and make sure the right people review them.

today.trigger: A reporting deadline approaches or the Finance Director requests a special budget report.
steps: Agree the audience, questions, scope, and deadline.
Ask colleagues and site managers for inputs and explanations.
Check that submissions use consistent periods and definitions.
Assemble the Excel, Power BI, and PowerPoint outputs.
Review the pack with the Controller or Finance Director and release the agreed version.
drudgery: Copying tables and charts into slides
today.time_sinks: Late contributions, changing report scope, and repeated review rounds involving several owners.

lenses.faster: Generate standard tables and charts from one validated snapshot. Use a shared input queue and draft commentary to reduce assembly and chasing.
lenses.autonomous: The reporting calendar opens the input workflow; validated data produces a draft pack. Final publication waits for the named reviewer.
lenses.ambitious: Offer consistent site-level reports and faster special analyses using reusable definitions and traceable source data.
lenses.joy: Remove slide copying and status tracking. Keep the work of choosing the story and helping decision makers understand it.
lenses.options: Prepare a short director brief, a detailed site review, and an exception-only view from the same approved figures.
lenses.altitude: Own reporting definitions, review standards, and delivery reliability rather than supervising every formatting step.
reach: Controller: coordinate the management reporting pack.
Finance Director: prepare draft board and management financial briefings.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: coordinate consistent aggregate workforce metrics in financial reports.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst sets priorities, resolves conflicting explanations, and decides what the audience needs to understand or act on.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: the workflow gathers inputs, builds outputs, handles missing contributions, and drafts commentary. Directing colleagues and approving the reporting narrative remain human responsibilities.

in_practice.trigger: A reporting-calendar milestone occurs or an authorised special-report brief is submitted.
steps: Create an input checklist from the report brief, owners, and deadline.
Verify the AFAS extract and Power BI refresh, then freeze a reconciled reporting snapshot.
Generate approved tables and charts and collect owner explanations in the shared queue.
Draft the pack with evidence links, missing-input flags, and clearly labelled estimates.
The analyst resolves gaps and obtains the required review before releasing the versioned pack.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst reviews every pack; the Controller or Finance Director approves official publication according to the report's audience.
systems: Proposed company-approved language-model and report-generation services
data_needed: Report calendar, audience, scope, and owners
Approved financial metric definitions
Reconciled actuals, budget, and forecast snapshot
Standard report templates and access permissions
Owner explanations with source references
Publication and review requirements
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reporting register with input status, snapshot date, metric and template versions, review comments, approval, and published pack.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh, providing a basis for recurring report preparation.
Template-based report generation and source-linked commentary are plausible, but need integration and review.
The proposed reporting workflow, 60% labour saving, and two times elapsed speedup are untested and depend on input punctuality.

risks: A polished pack conceals a failed refresh, provisional figures, or missing contributions.
Different report components use different snapshots or metric definitions.
Sensitive workforce or financial information reaches an overly broad audience.
Automated assembly saves little elapsed time when late human inputs remain the main bottleneck.
research_questions: How much of the 108.8 annual hours is assembly versus coordination and review?
Which pack sections already have stable definitions and templates?
Can every published figure be traced to one approved snapshot?
Does the pilot reduce delivery time and review rounds without adding reporting corrections?

tasks.short: Reconcile project budgets with department and company funding, including emergency reserves.

today.trigger: A budget changes, a project receives funding, or an emergency reserve is proposed for use.
steps: Collect approved company, department, and project budget versions.
Map each project allocation to its parent budget and funding source.
Compare child allocations, spending, and reservations with parent limits.
Investigate duplicate allocations, missing mappings, and reserve movements.
Document reconciliations and request approval for required transfers.
drudgery: Checking whether reserves have been counted twice
today.time_sinks: Resolving inconsistent budget versions and ambiguous links between projects, departments, and reserve pots.

lenses.faster: Use a controlled parent-child budget mapping to calculate reconciliations and remaining funding automatically.
lenses.autonomous: Run the checks after an approved budget revision or validated nightly extract. Route only mapping failures, limit breaches, and unauthorised movements to the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a complete view of where each approved euro is allocated, reserved, spent, or still available across all three sites.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet matching and repeated addition. Keep the investigation of genuine funding conflicts and reserve needs.
lenses.options: Calculate alternative transfers between eligible funding pots while showing the effect on headroom and reserve coverage.
lenses.altitude: Own the funding hierarchy, reserve rules, and reconciliation controls rather than matching allocations manually.
reach: Controller: maintain budget hierarchy controls.
Accountant: prepare reconciled funding schedules for audit support.
Finance Director: monitor reserve headroom and proposed transfers.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst interprets funding restrictions and judges whether using an emergency reserve is justified.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: this public-sector O*NET wording translates here to internal funding pots. Mapping, roll-ups, conservation of totals, and duplicate checks are explicit rules; reserve releases need approval.

in_practice.trigger: An approved budget version changes or a validated actuals and reservation snapshot becomes available.
steps: Load approved budget versions, actuals, commitments, and reservations.
Validate unique project mappings and reject missing parents or circular relationships.
Reconcile allocations and available funding at project, department, site, and company levels.
Apply reserve and transfer restrictions and record routine passes or exception cases.
The analyst resolves exceptions; the authorised approver approves transfers before the funding register changes.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine reconciliations run unattended; the analyst resolves exceptions and the Finance Director or delegated owner approves reserve releases and transfers.
data_needed: Approved parent-child budget hierarchy
Unique project and funding-source identifiers
Budget versions and effective dates
Actuals, commitments, and funding reservations
Reserve restrictions and transfer approval limits
Approved transfer history
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint funding reconciliation register with input versions, mapping checks, control totals, exceptions, approved transfers, and before-and-after balances.

evidence.claim: Power Query supports matching tables by one or more columns, useful for budget hierarchy reconciliation.
Budget hierarchy checks, duplicate detection, and transfer conservation checks can run as deterministic software.
The proposed reconciliation workflow, 80% labour saving, and four times elapsed speedup require a stable funding hierarchy and remain untested.

risks: A project mapped to multiple funding sources is counted twice.
Concurrent reserve requests exceed available headroom unless reservations are controlled.
Internal budgets, cash availability, and accounting provisions are treated as interchangeable.
A mapping error spreads through every roll-up and creates false assurance.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven actually maintain project funding pots and emergency reserves corresponding to this task?
Is there one approved parent-child hierarchy with unique identifiers and version history?
Can historical reserve movements and transfers be reconciled without undocumented adjustments?
Does a pilot detect seeded duplicate, missing-parent, and over-allocation cases while reproducing approved control totals?

role.altitude: The FP&A Analyst becomes the owner of the cost-driver model, forecast assumptions, and management decision evidence. Routine preparation runs through controlled software, while the analyst challenges managers and improves forecast reliability.
reach: Controller: management reporting, variance explanations, allocation controls, and funding reconciliations.
Finance Director: scenario preparation, investment prioritisation, and early financial warnings.
Accountant: candidate accrual gaps and supporting schedules, with journal approval retained by Accounting.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: aggregate workforce-cost planning using shared definitions.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: financial scenarios for approved CAO and benefit changes.
Learning and Development Specialist: project training costs and certification capacity planning.
role.ceiling_note: Current workflows and anatomy percentages are inferred from the supplied context, not observed. The eight tasks cover 1,133.5 hours per FTE per year, about 71% of a 1,600-hour role. The estimates imply about 1,524 annual labour hours released across both analysts, approximately 0.95 FTE or EUR 122,000 of capacity at EUR 80/hour, before setup, maintenance, and overlapping savings; this is not a cash-saving forecast. Time saved measures labour effort; speedup estimates elapsed completion time, including automation and human waits. Missing operational feeds, agency export access, late close entries, and specialist approvals limit gains. SAP, Adaptive Planning, Access, and VBA are not assumed to be installed. Re-integration decisions under Wet verbetering poortwachter remain with HR and qualified advisers; FP&A models permitted aggregate financial effects. Employer access to sickness information is restricted. [UWV re-integration guidance](https://www.uwv.nl/nl/ziek/re-integratie/samenwerking-werknemer-werkgever?friendlyurl=%2Fre-integratie), [AP employer sickness-data rules](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers). Any extension into individual worker evaluation, task allocation, or employment decisions requires a separate EU AI Act assessment. [European Commission AI Act guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)
skills_to_grow: Build and test financial models using Excel Power Query and, where available, SQL.
Define operational drivers with site managers and distinguish causes from correlations.
Backtest forecasts and explain uncertainty in concrete business terms.
Maintain effective-dated CAO assumptions with Payroll and HR.
Design reconciliations, exception thresholds, approval gates, and reproducible evidence.
Review language-model drafts against source records and restrict sensitive data.
Challenge investment benefits and negotiate credible assumptions with managers.
Measure handling time, elapsed time, forecast error, and audit corrections during pilots.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly, driver-based financial outlook for Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo using reconciled actuals, aggregate workforce costs, agency commitments, and validated operating volumes. Give managers tested options for seasonal demand, labour costs, investment timing, and cash needs; track forecast errors and realised benefits after each decision. Judge success by fewer days to close with a forecast managers trust, without more audit adjustments, rather than by the number of reports produced.
